Alyssa (Customer): Hey -- since ~10:12 UTC our API traffic from eu-west-1 is getting routed to us-west-2 and we're seeing 500/503 spikes + extra 250-400ms latency. Request IDs: req-abc123, req-abc124. Also noticed billing allocations show volume attributed to us-west. Any idea?

Support Bot: Thanks for the report, Alyssa — team has been notified and a human will follow up shortly :rotating_light:

Maria (Support): Sorry about that. Can you paste a quick curl that repros + the response headers you see? Also which customer cluster id/tenant ID is this?

Alyssa (Customer): repro below (from eu-west host):
```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' 'https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate' -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
Response headers include:
- HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
- x-request-id: req-abc123
- x-region: us-west-2
- via: envoy

Maria (Support): Hmm x-region set to us-west-2 is suspicious if the client is eu-west-1. Kevin / Edge team can you take a look?

Kevin (Edge): I'm seeing similar reports from a couple customers. Early hypothesis: when the L7 gateway fails over to the fallback cluster we accidentally preserve upstream-injected headers (x-region) instead of clearing them. That makes downstream think the request originated in us-west and sticky routing + billing tags are applied incorrectly.

Samir (Eng): That matches a recent change in the host_rewrite/route filter we shipped last week. Envoy has a header_inheritance behavior if route filters use internal redirects. If our filter chain doesn't explicitly remove 'x-region' or 'x-origin' before proxying to the fallback cluster, it will be copied.

Ron SRE: Temporary mitigation: you can disable cross-region fallback for this customer by setting route metadata in the Console -> Customers -> <tenant> -> routing -> prefer_same_region=true. That will avoid the fallback path and keep traffic local until we patch. Maria, can you apply that for Alyssa's tenant?

Maria (Support): Applied prefer_same_region=true for tenant-id t-9834. Please confirm if you still see the issue after a minute.

Alyssa (Customer): Confirmed: latency dropped back to expected, and 503 volume stopped. Billing is still showing a few misattributed tokens from earlier this morning though. Is that reversible?

Kevin (Edge): We'll need to run a small billing reconciliation job to reclassify those requests based on original X-Request-Region if our logs show the true origin. I'll coordinate with finance ops. For the root cause fix: short-term hotfix is to add a request header removal in the L7 path. Example Envoy config snippet we can apply as a hotpatch:
```yaml
- name: envoy.filters.http.header_to_remove
  typed_config: {}
  remove_request_headers: [ 'x-region', 'x-origin', 'x-client-region' ]
```
This will strip the problematic headers before proxying to fallback.

Samir (Eng): Adding note: hotpatch is low risk but we should also revert the change that introduced header inheritance and add an integration test that runs a fallback scenario asserting headers are cleared. Kevin, can you open the PR and link to this thread?

Deploy Bot: deploy v1.4.8-hotfix started by Maria at 2024-11-07T11:15:00Z -> rollout to gateway-l7 (canary 10%)

Kevin (Edge): PR created: revert of host_rewrite header-preserve logic + test. We'll merge after canary looks good. Plan: roll back to stable path on failure, otherwise full rollout in 30m.

Ron SRE: For the immediate customer impact, we've scheduled a billing reconciliation window 12:00-12:30 UTC. Finance ops will confirm adjustments.

Alyssa (Customer): Thanks all, appreciate the quick workaround and the hotfix timeline. Please ping here when fully rolled out.

Maria (Support): Will do. Also adding action items: (1) confirm hotfix completed and full rollout, (2) run reconciler and confirm billing changes, (3) add test to prevent header inheritance regressions.

Kevin (Edge): Noted. Follow-up: tests will include a scenario with upstream-injected x-region + fallback cluster, assert removed headers and correct region tag.

Support Bot: Issue update: severity=high, status=in-progress, incident_id=INC-20241107-47
